text_en: Now the word of the Lord came to Jonas, the son of Amathi, saying:
text_la: Et factum est verbum Domini ad Jonam, filium Amathi, dicens:
text_pt: E veio a palavra do SENHOR a Jonas, filho de Amitai, dizendo:
text_el: καὶ ἐγένετο λόγος κυρίου πρὸς Ιωναν τὸν τοῦ Αμαθι λέγων

text_en: Arise and go to Ninive, the great city, and preach in it: For the wickedness thereof has come up before me.
text_la: Surge, et vade in Niniven, civitatem grandem, et prædica in ea, quia ascendit malitia ejus coram me.
text_pt: Levanta-te, vai à grande cidade de Nínive, e clama contra ela, porque a sua malícia subiu até à minha presença.
text_el: ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύθητι εἰς Νινευη τὴν πόλιν τὴν μεγάλην καὶ κήρυξον ἐν αὐτῇ ὅτι ἀνέβη ἡ κραυγὴ τῆς κακίας αὐτῆς πρός με

text_en: And Jonas rose up to flee into Tharsis from the face of the Lord , and he went down to Joppe , and found a ship going to Tharsis: and he paid the fare thereof, and went down into it, to go with them to Tharsis from the face of the Lord ,
text_la: Et surrexit Jonas, ut fugeret in Tharsis a facie Domini, et descendit in Joppen : et invenit navem euntem in Tharsis, et dedit naulum ejus, et descendit in eam ut iret cum eis in Tharsis a facie Domini.
text_pt: Porém, Jonas se levantou para fugir da presença do Senhor para Társis. E descendo a Jope, achou um navio que ia para Társis; pagou, pois, a sua passagem, e desceu para dentro dele, para ir com eles para Társis, para longe da presença do Senhor.
text_el: καὶ ἀνέστη Ιωνας τοῦ φυγεῖν εἰς Θαρσις ἐκ προσώπου κυρίου καὶ κατέβη εἰς Ιοππην καὶ εὗρεν πλοῖον βαδίζον εἰς Θαρσις καὶ ἔδωκεν τὸ ναῦλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐνέβη εἰς αὐτὸ τοῦ πλεῦσαι μετ' αὐτῶν εἰς Θαρσις ἐκ προσώπου κυρίου

text_en: but the Lord sent a great wind to the sea: and a great tempest was raised in the sea, and the ship was in danger to be broken.
text_la: Dominus autem misit ventum magnum in mare : et facta est tempestas magna in mari, et navis periclitabatur conteri.
text_pt: Mas o Senhor mandou ao mar um grande vento, e fez-se no mar uma forte tempestade, e o navio estava a ponto de quebrar-se.
text_el: καὶ κύριος ἐξήγειρεν πνεῦμα εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐγένετο κλύδων μέγας ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ καὶ τὸ πλοῖον ἐκινδύνευεν συντριβῆναι

text_en: And the mariners were afraid, and the men cried to their god: and they cast forth the wares that were in the ship, into the sea, to lighten it of them: and Jonas went down into the inner part of the ship, and fell into a deep sleep.
text_la: Et timuerunt nautæ, et clamaverunt viri ad deum suum, et miserunt vasa quæ erant in navi, in mare, ut alleviaretur ab eis; et Jonas descendit ad interiora navis, et dormiebat sopore gravi.
text_pt: Então temeram os marinheiros, e clamavam cada um ao seu deus, e lançaram ao mar as cargas, que estavam no navio, para o aliviarem do seu peso; Jonas, porém, desceu ao porão do navio, e, tendo-se deitado, dormia um profundo sono.
text_el: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν οἱ ναυτικοὶ καὶ ἀνεβόων ἕκαστος πρὸς τὸν θεὸν αὐτῶν καὶ ἐκβολὴν ἐποιήσαντο τῶν σκευῶν τῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν τοῦ κουφισθῆναι ἀπ' αὐτῶν Ιωνας δὲ κατέβη εἰς τὴν κοίλην τοῦ πλοίου καὶ ἐκάθευδεν καὶ ἔρρεγχεν

text_en: And the shipmaster came to him and said to him: Why are you fast asleep? Rise up call upon your God , if so be that God will think of us that we may not perish.
text_la: Et accessit ad eum gubernator, et dixit ei : Quid tu sopore deprimeris? surge, invoca Deum tuum, si forte recogitet Deus de nobis, et non pereamus.
text_pt: E o mestre do navio chegou- se a ele, e disse-lhe: Que tens, dorminhoco? Levanta-te, clama ao teu Deus; talvez assim ele se lembre de nós para que não pereçamos.
text_el: καὶ προσῆλθεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ πρωρεὺς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ τί σὺ ῥέγχεις ἀνάστα καὶ ἐπικαλοῦ τὸν θεόν σου ὅπως διασώσῃ ὁ θεὸς ἡμᾶς καὶ μὴ ἀπολώμεθα

text_en: And they said every one to his fellow: Come and let us cast lots, that we may know why this evil is upon us. And they cast lots, and the lot fell upon Jonas.
text_la: Et dixit vir ad collegam suum : Venite et mittamus sortes, et sciamus quare hoc malum sit nobis. Et miserunt sortes, et cecidit sors super Jonam.
text_pt: E diziam cada um ao seu companheiro: Vinde, e lancemos sortes, para que saibamos por que causa nos sobreveio este mal. E lançaram sortes, e a sorte caiu sobre Jonas.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν ἕκαστος πρὸς τὸν πλησίον αὐτοῦ δεῦτε βάλωμεν κλήρους καὶ ἐπιγνῶμεν τίνος ἕνεκεν ἡ κακία αὕτη ἐστὶν ἐν ἡμῖν καὶ ἔβαλον κλήρους καὶ ἔπεσεν ὁ κλῆρος ἐπὶ Ιωναν

text_en: And they said to him: Tell us for what cause this evil is upon us, what is your business? Of what country are you? And where are you going? Or of what people are you?
text_la: Et dixerunt ad eum : Indica nobis cujus causa malum istud sit nobis : quod est opus tuum? quæ terra tua, et quo vadis? vel ex quo populo es tu?
text_pt: Então lhe disseram: Declara-nos tu agora, por causa de quem nos sobreveio este mal. Que ocupação é a tua? Donde vens? Qual é a tua terra? E de que povo és tu?
text_el: καὶ εἶπον πρὸς αὐτόν ἀπάγγειλον ἡμῖν τίνος ἕνεκεν ἡ κακία αὕτη ἐστὶν ἐν ἡμῖν τίς σου ἡ ἐργασία ἐστίν καὶ πόθεν ἔρχῃ καὶ ἐκ ποίας χώρας καὶ ἐκ ποίου λαοῦ εἶ σύ

text_en: And he said to them: I am a Hebrew , and I fear the Lord , and the God of heaven , who made both the sea and the dry land.
text_la: Et dixit ad eos : Hebræus ego sum, et Dominum Deum cæli ego timeo, qui fecit mare et aridam.
text_pt: E ele lhes disse: Eu sou hebreu, e temo ao Senhor, o Deus do céu, que fez o mar e a terra seca.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς δοῦλος κυρίου ἐγώ εἰμι καὶ τὸν κύριον θεὸν τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἐγὼ σέβομαι ὃς ἐποίησεν τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ τὴν ξηράν

text_en: And the men were greatly afraid, and they said to him: Why have you done this? (For the men knew that he fled from the face of the Lord : because he had told them.)
text_la: Et timuerunt viri timore magno, et dixerunt ad eum : Quid hoc fecisti? cognoverunt enim viri quod a facie Domini fugeret, quia indicaverat eis.
text_pt: Então estes homens se enche-ram de grande temor, e disseram-lhe: Por que fizeste tu isto? Pois sabiam os homens que fugia da presença do Senhor, porque ele lho tinha declarado.
text_el: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν οἱ ἄνδρες φόβον μέγαν καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν τί τοῦτο ἐποίησας διότι ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἄνδρες ὅτι ἐκ προσώπου κυρίου ἦν φεύγων ὅτι ἀπήγγειλεν αὐτοῖς

text_en: And they said to him: What shall we do with you, that the sea may be calm to us? For the sea flowed and swelled.
text_la: Et dixerunt ad eum : Quid faciemus tibi, et cessabit mare a nobis? quia mare ibat, et intumescebat.
text_pt: E disseram-lhe: Que te faremos nós, para que o mar se nos acalme? Porque o mar ia se tornando cada vez mais tempestuoso.
text_el: καὶ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν τί σοι ποιήσωμεν καὶ κοπάσει ἡ θάλασσα ἀφ' ἡμῶν ὅτι ἡ θάλασσα ἐπορεύετο καὶ ἐξήγειρεν μᾶλλον κλύδωνα

text_en: And he said to them: take me up, and cast me into the sea, and the sea shall be calm to you: for I know for my sake this great tempest is upon you.
text_la: Et dixit ad eos : Tollite me, et mittite in mare, et cessabit mare a vobis : scio enim ego quoniam propter me tempestas hæc grandis venit super vos.
text_pt: E ele lhes disse: Levantai-me, e lançai-me ao mar, e o mar se vos aquietará; porque eu sei que por minha causa vos sobreveio esta grande tempestade.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν Ιωνας πρὸς αὐτούς ἄρατέ με καὶ ἐμβάλετέ με εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ κοπάσει ἡ θάλασσα ἀφ' ὑμῶν διότι ἔγνωκα ἐγὼ ὅτι δι' ἐμὲ ὁ κλύδων ὁ μέγας οὗτος ἐφ' ὑμᾶς ἐστιν

text_en: And the men rowed hard to return to the land, but they were not able: because the sea tossed and swelled upon them.
text_la: Et remigabant viri ut reverterentur ad aridam, et non valebant, quia mare ibat, et intumescebat super eos.
text_pt: Entretanto, os homens remavam, para fazer voltar o navio à terra, mas não podiam, porquanto o mar se ia embravecendo cada vez mais contra eles.
text_el: καὶ παρεβιάζοντο οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ ἐπιστρέψαι πρὸς τὴν γῆν καὶ οὐκ ἠδύναντο ὅτι ἡ θάλασσα ἐπορεύετο καὶ ἐξηγείρετο μᾶλλον ἐπ' αὐτούς

text_en: And they cried to the Lord , and said: We beseech you, O Lord let us not perish for this man's life, and lay not upon us innocent blood: for you, O Lord , have done as it pleased you.
text_la: Et clamaverunt ad Dominum, et dixerunt : Quæsumus, Domine, ne pereamus in anima viri istius, et ne des super nos sanguinem innocentem : quia tu, Domine, sicut voluisti, fecisti.
text_pt: Então clamaram ao Senhor, e disseram: Ah, Senhor! Nós te rogamos, que não pereçamos por causa da alma deste homem, e que não ponhas sobre nós o sangue inocente; porque tu, Senhor, fizeste como te aprouve.
text_el: καὶ ἀνεβόησαν πρὸς κύριον καὶ εἶπαν μηδαμῶς κύριε μὴ ἀπολώμεθα ἕνεκεν τῆς ψυχῆς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου τούτου καὶ μὴ δῷς ἐφ' ἡμᾶς αἷμα δίκαιον ὅτι σύ κύριε ὃν τρόπον ἐβούλου πεποίηκας

text_en: And they took Jonas, and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceased from raging.
text_la: Et tulerunt Jonam, et miserunt in mare : et stetit mare a fervore suo.
text_pt: E levantaram a Jonas, e o lançaram ao mar, e cessou o mar da sua fúria.
text_el: καὶ ἔλαβον τὸν Ιωναν καὶ ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ ἔστη ἡ θάλασσα ἐκ τοῦ σάλου αὐτῆς

text_en: And the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and sacrificed victims to the Lord , and made vows .
text_la: Et timuerunt viri timore magno Dominum : et immolaverunt hostias Domino, et voverunt vota.
text_pt: Temeram, pois, estes homens ao Senhor com grande temor; e ofereceram sacrifício ao Senhor, e fizeram votos.
text_el: καὶ ἐφοβήθησαν οἱ ἄνδρες φόβῳ μεγάλῳ τὸν κύριον καὶ ἔθυσαν θυσίαν τῷ κυρίῳ καὶ εὔξαντο εὐχάς

text_en: Now the Lord prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonas: and Jonas was in the belly of a fish for three days and three nights.
text_la: Et præparavit Dominus piscem grandem ut deglutiret Jonam : et erat Jonas in ventre piscis tribus diebus et tribus noctibus.
text_pt: E orou Jonas ao SENHOR, seu Deus, das entranhas do peixe.
text_el: καὶ προσέταξεν κύριος κήτει μεγάλῳ καταπιεῖν τὸν Ιωναν καὶ ἦν Ιωνας ἐν τῇ κοιλίᾳ τοῦ κήτους τρεῖς ἡμέρας καὶ τρεῖς νύκτας

text_en: And Jonas prayed to the Lord , his God , out of the belly of the fish.
text_la: Et oravit Jonas ad Dominum Deum suum de ventre piscis,
text_pt: E disse: Na minha angústia clamei ao Senhor, e ele me respondeu; do ventre do inferno gritei, e tu ouviste a minha voz.
text_el: καὶ προσηύξατο Ιωνας πρὸς κύριον τὸν θεὸν αὐτοῦ ἐκ τῆς κοιλίας τοῦ κήτους

text_en: And he said: I cried out of my affliction to the Lord , and he heard me: I cried out of the belly of hell, and you have heard my voice.
text_la: et dixit : Clamavi de tribulatione mea ad Dominum, et exaudivit me; de ventre inferi clamavi, et exaudisti vocem meam.
text_pt: Porque tu me lançaste no profundo, no coração dos mares, e a corrente das águas me cercou; todas as tuas ondas e as tuas vagas têm passado por cima de mim.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν ἐβόησα ἐν θλίψει μου πρὸς κύριον τὸν θεόν μου καὶ εἰσήκουσέν μου ἐκ κοιλίας ᾅδου κραυγῆς μου ἤκουσας φωνῆς μου

text_en: And you have cast me forth into the deep, in the heart of the sea, and a flood have compassed me: all your billows, and your waves have passed over me.
text_la: Et projecisti me in profundum in corde maris, et flumen circumdedit me : omnes gurgites tui, et fluctus tui super me transierunt.
text_pt: E eu disse: Lançado estou de diante dos teus olhos; todavia tornarei a ver o teu santo templo.
text_el: ἀπέρριψάς με εἰς βάθη καρδίας θαλάσσης καὶ ποταμοί με ἐκύκλωσαν πάντες οἱ μετεωρισμοί σου καὶ τὰ κύματά σου ἐπ' ἐμὲ διῆλθον

text_en: And I said: I am cast away out of the sight of your eyes: but yet I shall see your holy temple again.
text_la: Et ego dixi : Abjectus sum a conspectu oculorum tuorum; verumtamen rursus videbo templum sanctum tuum.
text_pt: As águas me cercaram até à alma, o abismo me rodeou, e as algas se enrolaram na minha cabeça.
text_el: καὶ ἐγὼ εἶπα ἀπῶσμαι ἐξ ὀφθαλμῶν σου ἆρα προσθήσω τοῦ ἐπιβλέψαι πρὸς τὸν ναὸν τὸν ἅγιόν σου

text_en: The waters compassed me about even to the soul : the deep has closed me round about, the sea has covered my head.
text_la: Circumdederunt me aquæ usque ad animam : abyssus vallavit me, pelagus operuit caput meum.
text_pt: Eu desci até aos fundamentos dos montes; a terra me encerrou para sempre com os seus ferrolhos; mas tu fizeste subir a minha vida da perdição, ó Senhor meu Deus.
text_el: περιεχύθη ὕδωρ μοι ἕως ψυχῆς ἄβυσσος ἐκύκλωσέν με ἐσχάτη ἔδυ ἡ κεφαλή μου εἰς σχισμὰς ὀρέων

text_en: I went down to the lowest parts of the mountains: the bars of the earth have shut me up for ever: and you will bring up my life from corruption, O Lord , my God .
text_la: Ad extrema montium descendi; terræ vectes concluserunt me in æternum : et sublevabis de corruptione vitam meam, Domine Deus meus.
text_pt: Quando desfalecia em mim a minha alma, lembrei-me do Senhor; e entrou a ti a minha oração, no teu santo templo.
text_el: κατέβην εἰς γῆν ἧς οἱ μοχλοὶ αὐτῆς κάτοχοι αἰώνιοι καὶ ἀναβήτω φθορὰ ζωῆς μου κύριε ὁ θεός μου

text_en: When my soul was in distress within me, I remembered the Lord : that my prayer may come to you, unto your holy temple .
text_la: Cum angustiaretur in me anima mea, Domini recordatus sum : ut veniat ad te oratio mea, ad templum sanctum tuum.
text_pt: Os que observam as falsas vaidades deixam a sua misericórdia.
text_el: ἐν τῷ ἐκλείπειν ἀπ' ἐμοῦ τὴν ψυχήν μου τοῦ κυρίου ἐμνήσθην καὶ ἔλθοι πρὸς σὲ ἡ προσευχή μου εἰς ναὸν ἅγιόν σου

text_en: They that in vain observe vanities, forsake their own mercy.
text_la: Qui custodiunt vanitates frustra, misericordiam suam derelinquunt.
text_pt: Mas eu te oferecerei sacrifício com a voz do agradecimento; o que votei pagarei. Do Senhor vem a salvação.
text_el: φυλασσόμενοι μάταια καὶ ψευδῆ ἔλεος αὐτῶν ἐγκατέλιπον

text_en: But I with the voice of praise will sacrifice to you: I will pay whatsoever I have vowed for my salvation to the Lord .
text_la: Ego autem in voce laudis immolabo tibi : quæcumque vovi, reddam pro salute Domino.
text_pt: Falou, pois, o Senhor ao peixe, e este vomitou a Jonas na terra seca.
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ μετὰ φωνῆς αἰνέσεως καὶ ἐξομολογήσεως θύσω σοι ὅσα ηὐξάμην ἀποδώσω σοι σωτηρίου τῷ κυρίῳ

text_en: And the Lord spoke to the fish: and it vomited out Jonas upon the dry land.
text_la: Et dixit Dominus pisci, et evomuit Jonam in aridam.
text_el: καὶ προσετάγη τῷ κήτει καὶ ἐξέβαλεν τὸν Ιωναν ἐπὶ τὴν ξηράν

text_en: And the word of the Lord came to Jonas the second time saying:
text_la: Et factum est verbum Domini ad Jonam secundo, dicens:
text_pt: E veio a palavra do SENHOR segunda vez a Jonas, dizendo:
text_el: καὶ ἐγένετο λόγος κυρίου πρὸς Ιωναν ἐκ δευτέρου λέγων

text_en: Arise, and go to Ninive, the great city: and preach in it the preaching that I bid you.
text_la: Surge, et vade in Niniven, civitatem magnam, et prædica in ea prædicationem quam ego loquor ad te.
text_pt: Levanta-te, e vai à grande cidade de Nínive, e prega contra ela a mensagem que eu te digo.
text_el: ἀνάστηθι καὶ πορεύθητι εἰς Νινευη τὴν πόλιν τὴν μεγάλην καὶ κήρυξον ἐν αὐτῇ κατὰ τὸ κήρυγμα τὸ ἔμπροσθεν ὃ ἐγὼ ἐλάλησα πρὸς σέ

text_en: And Jonas arose, and went to Ninive, according to the word of the Lord : now Ninive was a great city of three days' journey.
text_la: Et surrexit Jonas, et abiit in Niniven juxta verbum Domini : et Ninive erat civitas magna, itinere trium dierum.
text_pt: E levantou-se Jonas, e foi a Nínive, segundo a palavra do Senhor. Ora, Nínive era uma cidade muito grande, de três dias de caminho.
text_el: καὶ ἀνέστη Ιωνας καὶ ἐπορεύθη εἰς Νινευη καθὼς ἐλάλησεν κύριος ἡ δὲ Νινευη ἦν πόλις μεγάλη τῷ θεῷ ὡσεὶ πορείας ὁδοῦ ἡμερῶν τριῶν

text_en: And Jonas began to enter into the city one day's journey: and he cried and said: Yet forty days and Ninive shall be destroyed.
text_la: Et cœpit Jonas introire in civitatem itinere diei unius : et clamavit, et dixit : Adhuc quadraginta dies, et Ninive subvertetur.
text_pt: E começou Jonas a entrar pela cidade caminho de um dia, e pregava, dizendo: Ainda quarenta dias, e Nínive será subvertida.
text_el: καὶ ἤρξατο Ιωνας τοῦ εἰσελθεῖν εἰς τὴν πόλιν ὡσεὶ πορείαν ἡμέρας μιᾶς καὶ ἐκήρυξεν καὶ εἶπεν ἔτι τρεῖς ἡμέραι καὶ Νινευη καταστραφήσεται

text_en: And the men of Ninive believed in God : and they proclaimed a fast , and put on sackcloth from the greatest to the least.
text_la: Et crediderunt viri Ninivitæ in Deum, et prædicaverunt jejunium, et vestiti sunt saccis, a majore usque ad minorem.
text_pt: E os homens de Nínive creram em Deus; e proclamaram um jejum, e vestiram-se de saco, desde o maior até ao menor.
text_el: καὶ ἐνεπίστευσαν οἱ ἄνδρες Νινευη τῷ θεῷ καὶ ἐκήρυξαν νηστείαν καὶ ἐνεδύσαντο σάκκους ἀπὸ μεγάλου αὐτῶν ἕως μικροῦ αὐτῶν

text_en: And the word came to the king of Ninive: and he rose up out of his throne, and cast away his robe from him, and was clothed in sackcloth , and sat in ashes.
text_la: Et pervenit verbum ad regem Ninive : et surrexit de solio suo, et abjecit vestimentum suum a se, et indutus est sacco, et sedit in cinere.
text_pt: Esta palavra chegou também ao rei de Nínive; e ele levantou-se do seu trono, e tirou de si as suas vestes, e cobriu-se de saco, e sentou-se sobre a cinza.
text_el: καὶ ἤγγισεν ὁ λόγος πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα τῆς Νινευη καὶ ἐξανέστη ἀπὸ τοῦ θρόνου αὐτοῦ καὶ περιείλατο τὴν στολὴν αὐτοῦ ἀφ' ἑαυτοῦ καὶ περιεβάλετο σάκκον καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐπὶ σποδοῦ

text_en: And he caused it to be proclaimed and published in Ninive, from the mouth of the king and of his princes, saying: Let neither men nor beasts, oxen, nor sheep taste anything: let them not feed, nor drink water.
text_la: Et clamavit, et dixit in Ninive ex ore regis et principum ejus, dicens : Homines, et jumenta, et boves, et pecora non gustent quidquam : nec pascantur, et aquam non bibant.
text_pt: E fez uma proclamação que se divulgou em Nínive, pelo decreto do rei e dos seus grandes, dizendo: Nem homens, nem animais, nem bois, nem ovelhas provem coisa alguma, nem se lhes dê alimentos, nem bebam água;
text_el: καὶ ἐκηρύχθη καὶ ἐρρέθη ἐν τῇ Νινευη παρὰ τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ παρὰ τῶν μεγιστάνων αὐτοῦ λέγων οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ τὰ κτήνη καὶ οἱ βόες καὶ τὰ πρόβατα μὴ γευσάσθωσαν μηδὲν μηδὲ νεμέσθωσαν μηδὲ ὕδωρ πιέτωσαν

text_en: And let men and beasts be covered with sackcloth , and cry to the Lord with all their strength, and let them turn every one from his evil way, and from the iniquity that is in their hands.
text_la: Et operiantur saccis homines et jumenta, et clament ad Dominum in fortitudine : et convertatur vir a via sua mala, et ab iniquitate quæ est in manibus eorum.
text_pt: Mas os homens e os animais sejam cobertos de sacos, e clamem fortemente a Deus, e convertam-se, cada um do seu mau caminho, e da violência que há nas suas mãos.
text_el: καὶ περιεβάλοντο σάκκους οἱ ἄνθρωποι καὶ τὰ κτήνη καὶ ἀνεβόησαν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ἐκτενῶς καὶ ἀπέστρεψαν ἕκαστος ἀπὸ τῆς ὁδοῦ αὐτοῦ τῆς πονηρᾶς καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς ἀδικίας τῆς ἐν χερσὶν αὐτῶν λέγοντες

text_en: Who can tell if God will turn, and forgive: and will turn away from his fierce anger , and we shall not perish?
text_la: Quis scit si convertatur et ignoscat Deus, et revertatur a furore iræ suæ, et non peribimus?
text_pt: Quem sabe se se voltará Deus, e se arrependerá, e se apartará do furor da sua ira, de sorte que não pereçamos?
text_el: τίς οἶδεν εἰ μετανοήσει ὁ θεὸς καὶ ἀποστρέψει ἐξ ὀργῆς θυμοῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ οὐ μὴ ἀπολώμεθα

text_en: And God saw their works, that they were turned from their evil way: and God had mercy with regard to the evil which he had said that he would do to them, and he did it not.
text_la: Et vidit Deus opera eorum, quia conversi sunt de via sua mala : et misertus est Deus super malitiam quam locutus fuerat ut faceret eis, et non fecit.
text_pt: E Deus viu as obras deles, como se converteram do seu mau caminho; e Deus se arrependeu do mal que tinha anunciado lhes faria, e não o fez.
text_el: καὶ εἶδεν ὁ θεὸς τὰ ἔργα αὐτῶν ὅτι ἀπέστρεψαν ἀπὸ τῶν ὁδῶν αὐτῶν τῶν πονηρῶν καὶ μετενόησεν ὁ θεὸς ἐπὶ τῇ κακίᾳ ᾗ ἐλάλησεν τοῦ ποιῆσαι αὐτοῖς καὶ οὐκ ἐποίησεν

text_en: And Jonas was exceedingly troubled, and was angry :
text_la: Et afflictus est Jonas afflictione magna, et iratus est:
text_pt: Mas isso desagradou extremamente a Jonas, e ele ficou irado.
text_el: καὶ ἐλυπήθη Ιωνας λύπην μεγάλην καὶ συνεχύθη

text_en: And he prayed to the Lord , and said: I beseech you, O Lord , is not this what I said, when I was yet in my own country? Therefore I went before to flee into Tharsis: for I know that you are a gracious and merciful God , patient, and of much compassion, and easy to forgive evil .
text_la: et oravit ad Dominum, et dixit : Obsecro, Domine, numquid non hoc est verbum meum cum adhuc essem in terra mea? propter hoc præoccupavi ut fugerem in Tharsis : scio enim quia tu Deus clemens et misericors es, patiens et multæ miserationis, et ignoscens super malitia.
text_pt: E orou ao Senhor, e disse: Ah! Senhor! Não foi esta minha palavra, estando ainda na minha terra? Por isso é que me preveni, fugindo para Társis, pois sabia que és Deus compassivo e misericordioso, longânimo e grande em benignidade, e que te arrependes do mal.
text_el: καὶ προσεύξατο πρὸς κύριον καὶ εἶπεν ὦ κύριε οὐχ οὗτοι οἱ λόγοι μου ἔτι ὄντος μου ἐν τῇ γῇ μου διὰ τοῦτο προέφθασα τοῦ φυγεῖν εἰς Θαρσις διότι ἔγνων ὅτι σὺ ἐλεήμων καὶ οἰκτίρμων μακρόθυμος καὶ πολυέλεος καὶ μετανοῶν ἐπὶ ταῖς κακίαις

text_en: And now, O Lord , I beseech you take my life from me: for it is better for me to die than to live.
text_la: Et nunc, Domine, tolle, quæso, animam meam a me, quia melior est mihi mors quam vita.
text_pt: Peço-te, pois, ó Senhor, tira-me a vida, porque melhor me é morrer do que viver.
text_el: καὶ νῦν δέσποτα κύριε λαβὲ τὴν ψυχήν μου ἀπ' ἐμοῦ ὅτι καλὸν τὸ ἀποθανεῖν με ἢ ζῆν με

text_en: And the Lord said: Do you think you have reason to be angry ?
text_la: Et dixit Dominus : Putasne bene irasceris tu?
text_pt: E disse o Senhor: Fazes bem que assim te ires?
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος πρὸς Ιωναν εἰ σφόδρα λελύπησαι σύ

text_en: Then Jonas went out of the city, and sat toward the east side of the city: and he made himself a booth there, and he sat under it in the shadow, till he might see what would befall the city.
text_la: Et egressus est Jonas de civitate, et sedit contra orientem civitatis : et fecit sibimet umbraculum ibi, et sedebat subter illud in umbra, donec videret quid accideret civitati.
text_pt: Então Jonas saiu da cidade, e sentou-se ao oriente dela; e ali fez uma cabana, e sentou-se debaixo dela, à sombra, até ver o que aconteceria à cidade.
text_el: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν Ιωνας ἐκ τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἀπέναντι τῆς πόλεως καὶ ἐποίησεν ἑαυτῷ ἐκεῖ σκηνὴν καὶ ἐκάθητο ὑποκάτω αὐτῆς ἐν σκιᾷ ἕως οὗ ἀπίδῃ τί ἔσται τῇ πόλει

text_en: And the Lord God prepared an ivy, and it came up over the head of Jonas, to be a shadow over his head, and to cover him (for he was fatigued): and Jonas was exceeding glad of the ivy.
text_la: Et præparavit Dominus Deus hederam, et ascendit super caput Jonæ, ut esset umbra super caput ejus, et protegeret eum (laboraverat enim) : et lætatus est Jonas super hedera lætitia magna.
text_pt: E fez o Senhor Deus nascer uma aboboreira, e ela subiu por cima de Jonas, para que fizesse sombra sobre a sua cabeça, a fim de o livrar do seu enfado; e Jonas se alegrou em extremo por causa da aboboreira.
text_el: καὶ προσέταξεν κύριος ὁ θεὸς κολοκύνθῃ καὶ ἀνέβη ὑπὲρ κεφαλῆς τοῦ Ιωνα τοῦ εἶναι σκιὰν ὑπεράνω τῆς κεφαλῆς αὐτοῦ τοῦ σκιάζειν αὐτῷ ἀπὸ τῶν κακῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐχάρη Ιωνας ἐπὶ τῇ κολοκύνθῃ χαρὰν μεγάλην

text_en: But God prepared a worm, when the morning arose on the following day: and it struck the ivy and it withered.
text_la: Et paravit Deus vermen ascensu diluculi in crastinum : et percussit hederam, et exaruit.
text_pt: Mas Deus enviou um verme, no dia seguinte ao subir da alva, o qual feriu a aboboreira, e esta se secou.
text_el: καὶ προσέταξεν ὁ θεὸς σκώληκι ἑωθινῇ τῇ ἐπαύριον καὶ ἐπάταξεν τὴν κολόκυνθαν καὶ ἀπεξηράνθη

text_en: And when the sun was risen, the Lord commanded a hot and burning wind: and the sun beat upon the head of Jonas, and he broiled with the heat: and he desired for his soul that he might die, and said: It is better for me to die than to live.
text_la: Et cum ortus fuisset sol, præcepit Dominus vento calido et urenti : et percussit sol super caput Jonæ, et æstuabat : et petivit animæ suæ ut moreretur, et dixit : Melius est mihi mori quam vivere.
text_pt: E aconteceu que, aparecendo o sol, Deus mandou um vento calmoso oriental, e o sol feriu a cabeça de Jonas; e ele desmaiou, e desejou com toda a sua alma morrer, dizendo: Melhor me é morrer do que viver.
text_el: καὶ ἐγένετο ἅμα τῷ ἀνατεῖλαι τὸν ἥλιον καὶ προσέταξεν ὁ θεὸς πνεύματι καύσωνος συγκαίοντι καὶ ἐπάταξεν ὁ ἥλιος ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν Ιωνα καὶ ὠλιγοψύχησεν καὶ ἀπελέγετο τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν καλόν μοι ἀποθανεῖν με ἢ ζῆν

text_en: And the Lord said to Jonas: Do you think you have reason to be angry , for the ivy? And he said: I am angry with reason even unto death.
text_la: Et dixit Dominus ad Jonam : Putasne bene irasceris tu super hedera? Et dixit : Bene irascor ego usque ad mortem.
text_pt: Então disse Deus a Jonas: Fazes bem que assim te ires por causa da aboboreira? E ele disse: Faço bem que me revolte até à morte.
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς πρὸς Ιωναν εἰ σφόδρα λελύπησαι σὺ ἐπὶ τῇ κολοκύνθῃ καὶ εἶπεν σφόδρα λελύπημαι ἐγὼ ἕως θανάτου

text_en: And the Lord said: You are grieved for the ivy, for which you have not laboured, nor made it to grow, which in one night came up, and in one night perished.
text_la: Et dixit Dominus : Tu doles super hederam in qua non laborasti, neque fecisti ut cresceret; quæ sub una nocte nata est, et sub una nocte periit:
text_pt: E disse o Senhor: Tiveste tu compaixão da aboboreira, na qual não trabalhaste, nem a fizeste crescer, que numa noite nasceu, e numa noite pereceu;
text_el: καὶ εἶπεν κύριος σὺ ἐφείσω ὑπὲρ τῆς κολοκύνθης ὑπὲρ ἧς οὐκ ἐκακοπάθησας ἐπ' αὐτὴν καὶ οὐκ ἐξέθρεψας αὐτήν ἣ ἐγενήθη ὑπὸ νύκτα καὶ ὑπὸ νύκτα ἀπώλετο

text_en: And shall I not spare Ninive, that great city, in which there are more than a hundred and twenty thousand persons , that know how to distinguish between their right hand and their left, and many beasts?
text_la: et ego non parcam Ninive, civitati magnæ, in qua sunt plus quam centum viginti millia hominum qui nesciunt quid sit inter dexteram et sinistram suam, et jumenta multa?
text_pt: E não hei de eu ter compaixão da grande cidade de Nínive, em que estão mais de cento e vinte mil homens que não sabem discernir entre a sua mão direita e a sua mão esquerda, e também muitos animais?
text_el: ἐγὼ δὲ οὐ φείσομαι ὑπὲρ Νινευη τῆς πόλεως τῆς μεγάλης ἐν ᾗ κατοικοῦσιν πλείους ἢ δώδεκα μυριάδες ἀνθρώπων οἵτινες οὐκ ἔγνωσαν δεξιὰν αὐτῶν ἢ ἀριστερὰν αὐτῶν καὶ κτήνη πολλά
